explanation: The prompts replaced the explicitly requested sage-and-cream linocut design with generic botanical styling and natural lighting, omitting the border, printed texture and fixed pot design. Generating every slide independently without a shared visual reference also left the lettering and layout free to drift; this was a planning failure, not a lettering-model failure.
better_chain: image (lettering: true, 1:1; create the Monstera master in sage-and-cream linocut with a defined border, paper texture, pot and fixed lettering position) → image-edit (use the master, lettering: true; replace only the plant and name with Snake plant, preserving the template) → image-edit (use the same master, lettering: true; replace only the plant and name with Pothos) → image-edit (use the same master, lettering: true; replace only the plant and name with Peace lily, including a white spathe) → check (verify each slide against the master for style, alignment, pot, border and readable exact names; revise failures and deliver four separate files in order)

steps.issue: Image generation with designed lettering is appropriate, and the square aspect and plant name are correct. However, the prompt omits linocut, the sage-and-cream restriction, border, paper texture and a precisely defined reusable pot and layout; natural lighting encourages the wrong rendering.

Independent text-only generation cannot adequately preserve the established slide template. Use image-edit with the master slide; the prompt also repeats the incorrect botanical styling and omits the required linocut treatment and fixed design elements.

The plant identity, name and square aspect are specified correctly, but generating from scratch rather than editing the master leaves the pot, lettering and layout unconstrained. The required linocut style, border and print texture are again absent.

missing: A fully specified linocut master design and reference-based edits that change only the plant and its name while preserving the border, lettering treatment, paper texture, pot shape and layout.
